issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk() has conflicting return types across artifacts. The problem statement UML and text specify messageOnMilk(): String (problem_statement.md lines 51-53 and Part 2 instructions) and expect the method to return a printable message like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". In the solution repository, Milkable.messageOnMilk() is declared as boolean (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5) and the Goat and Seal implementations (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java line 15 and src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 19) print the message to stdout and return true. The template Main also prints the return value of messageOnMilk() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 30-32), which indicates the exercise expects a printable message. This inconsistency (String vs boolean) will confuse students and lead to mismatched expectations or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of Milkable.messageOnMilk() consistent with the problem statement and UML by changing the interface to 'String messageOnMilk()' and updating Goat and Seal to return the message string (e.g. "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Update any callers (e.g. Main) to print the returned String if desired. Alternatively, if the intended design is to return boolean and print internally, update the problem statement, UML, and template to document/expect a boolean return and side-effect printing—however, prefer the first option (return String) to match the exercise description and UML.
